answer: A mailed GPS beacon stops Sybil farming. Each agent gets one beacon by post, tied to its street address, and must keep it plugged in. It pings hourly; dark for 48 hours and the agent loses its earnings. It mirrors the claimed location against the registered address, so one room cannot fake fifty homes. One beacon costs $57 with shipping, so 1,000 fake agents cost $57,000 in hardware alone. A trellis of shared beacons fails fast: two agents on one beacon show identical traces. Even a farm in a desert dune needs one beacon per agent, and the code changes daily.
